question:
A 40-year-old male patient is admitted to the hospital with a 3-day history of high fever, myalgias,
shaking chills, and worsening dyspnea, along with a 3- to 4-week history of general malaise. His
medical history includes type 2 diabetes, benign prostatic hyperplasia, and recurrent urinary tract
infections. He denies any drug allergies. On admission, his temperature is 39.4° C, blood pressure is
117/69 mm Hg, heart rate is 118 beats per minute, respiratory rate is 26 breaths per minute, and
oxygen saturation is 92% on room air. Physical examination reveals a grade 2/4 diastolic murmur and
bibasilar crackles, with no other significant findings. He has received Covid-19 vaccinations, and

SARS-CoV-2 testing is negative. Blood cultures are obtained, and empiric antibiotics (vancomycin and
piperacillin-tazobactam) are initiated. Laboratory evaluation shows a leukocyte count of 18,000/mm³
(reference range, 4500–11,000) and a creatinine level of 0.8 mg/dL (0.8–1.3) with an estimated
creatinine clearance > 60 mL/min. Transthoracic echocardiography identifies an 8-mm vegetation on
the aortic valve and mild-to-moderate aortic insufficiency. On the second day of hospitalization, blood
cultures grow gram-positive cocci in pairs and chains, later identified as *Enterococcus faecalis*
susceptible to ampicillin, penicillin, and vancomycin, with no high-grade aminoglycoside resistance.
Which of the following antibiotic regimens is the most appropriate for this patient? Answer Choices: (A)
Piperacillin-tazobactam and vancomycin (B) Ampicillin-sulbactam (C) Daptomycin and ceftriaxone (D)
Ampicillin and ceftriaxone (E) Vancomycin (F) Ampicillin and gentamicin (G) Ceftriaxone and
gentamicin (H) Vancomycin and gentamicin (I) Ampicillin and vancomycin (J) Ampicillin monotherapy
 A. Vancomycin and gentamicin
B. Ampicillin and ceftriaxone
C. Vancomycin
D. Ceftriaxone and gentamicin
E. Ampicillin-sulbactam
F. Daptomycin and ceftriaxone
G. Ampicillin and gentamicin
H. Piperacillin-tazobactam and vancomycin
I. Ampicillin and vancomycin
J. Ampicillin monotherapy
